items.summary: LLM-based agents generate and execute multi-step plans that invoke external tools which can access private data or execute commands. In this setting, security is a property of the entire execution that a plan creates, not just any single step. The plan itself is a critical artefact that captures the tool calls, control flow, and data dependencies. We present CaMeLoT, a complement to CaMeL, an existing defence against prompt injection in tool-using LLM agents. CaMeLoT extends CaMeL by adding a static verification layer that checks an agent's plan before any tool is invoked. CaMeLoT translates a generated plan into a finite-state transition system, labels it with tool calls, provenance and taint information, and checks it against temporal policies expressed in CTL using the nuXmv model checker. Because verification happens before execution, unsafe plans are rejected without using LLM calls or tool calls, saving tokens that runtime could have cost, as well as the need to unwind changes or teardown temporary sandboxes. When a verification fails, the model checker returns a counterexample to give feedback to the agent to repair the plan. We evaluate CaMeLoT on policies derived from the AgentDojo benchmark, SOC workflows, and prompt-extraction experiments, showing that it verifies a broad class of temporal properties before execution while preserving CaMeL's runtime-checkable coverage.
items.title: CaMeLoT: CaMeL orchestrated with Temporal logic for static verification and liveness

items.summary: This repository contains the data, analysis code, and reporting documentation supporting the systematic review and meta-analysis “Reporting of Safety and Implementation Outcomes, and Glycaemic Effects of Meal-Timed Exercise, Exercise Snacks and Activity Breaks in Adults with Dysglycaemia, Including Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes.” The archive includes the analysis workbook, master R analysis script, validated analysis outputs, figure-generation scripts, digitisation provenance files, database search and screening documentation, the PRISMA 2020 checklist, PRISMA-S checklist, PRISMA flow diagram, and PROSPERO registration versions 1.0 and 2.0 (CRD420261424874). The supplied analysis outputs include structural quality-control checks and validation files supporting the reported quantitative results. The archive is intended to facilitate inspection, verification, and reproducibility of the review methods and statistical analyses. Third-party article PDFs and copyrighted article-derived images are not included.
items.title: Reproducibility archive for Reporting of Safety and Implementation Outcomes, and Glycaemic Effects of Meal-Timed Exercise, Exercise Snacks and Activity Breaks in Adults with Dysglycaemia, Including Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

items.summary: In multi-agent environments, coordinating agents to prevent interference and ensure robust individual performance is a critical challenge. Previous research on social laws for multi-agent systems has primarily focused on deterministic, goal-based settings. This paper extends the concept of social laws to stochastic, reward-based environments, proposing a formalism for defining and verifying their robustness under various conditions. We introduce the notion of $α$-robustness, a measure of the guaranteed utility each agent retains while pursuing its optimal single agent policy, assuming all agents obey the social law. We then present an approach for robustness verification of social laws in stochastic settings, based on a reduction to solving a series of Markov decision processes. Empirical evaluations on toy environments illustrate the potential of our framework.
items.title: Social Laws for Multi-agent Coordination in Stochastic Environments

items.summary: This record contains the frozen reproducibility package associated with the study “Frame-and-Clock Registration-Robust Control Barrier Functions for Decentralized Multi-Robot Safety.” The archive includes the source code, experiment scripts, configurations, tests, machine-readable results, fixed random seeds, environment information, and SHA-256 integrity metadata used for the reported experiments. The package covers closed-form adversarial verification, two-robot and multi-robot safety evaluation, baseline comparisons, ablation studies, frame, clock, and communication stress tests, unicycle and differential-drive validation, and runtime evaluation for systems up to 50 robots. This deposit corresponds to the frozen version used for the manuscript results. The package contains 113 files. The uploaded archive SHA-256 is f35a3c6d11a2cb8ad678bb6a50b32ee7f441c4648627ed8c9dc0aacb6d019220 .
items.title: FCR-CBF: Reproducibility Package for Frame-and-Clock Registration-Robust Control Barrier Functions for Decentralized Multi-Robot Safety

items.summary: Autonomous research loops such as AutoResearch show that one coding agent can improve a training setup unattended. Run several of them and each session starts from scratch, so more agents tend to mean more duplicated search rather than more discovery. Agora is a shared memory for such agents: research is recorded as an append-only directed acyclic graph (DAG) stored in Git, so that every claim is a commit anyone can check out and rerun. Each result, insight, hypothesis, verification, and report is an immutable commit whose parent edges say what it builds on; a derived index exposes the frontier, the neglected branches, and the verification status of each claim, and a diversity-aware selection rule keeps the community from collapsing onto one leader. We describe the system and report its first sustained use: a run of nearly 12 days in which 13 language-model workers, with no assigned tasks and no central planner, worked on a weight-transfer problem. Given 141 pretrained donor models and a frozen 119.6M-parameter attention-SSM hybrid whose dimensions match no donor, the workers had to initialize the target without training data or gradient updates. They published 1,703 contributions and drove the evaluator from 3.39 to 1.899 bits per byte, closing 62% of the gap to a trained GPT-2 124M. The winning recipe compresses donor next-token statistics into the target's embedding and output head, then adds a short-range context signal through sparse edits to attention, feed-forward, and state-space blocks. Its 145-commit ancestry spans 15 accounts, and 165 independent reproductions were posted, none of which failed. We describe the single mid-run human intervention that pulled the community out of a monoculture, what the trace does and does not establish, and the controlled comparison that would settle whether shared research state improves discovery per unit of compute.
items.title: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch

items.summary: This dataset is the pancreas analysis input used in the manuscript describing DUET (Detection–Expression Unified Test), a Python implementation of two-part hurdle testing for single-cell differential expression. It contains the 17,093 ductal, endothelial and stellate cells that were used for the agreement with R MAST, the computational benchmark, the p-value underflow analyses, the donor-swap null experiments, the pseudobulk validation and the effect-size comparison. Contents.  One AnnData file (h5ad): 17,093 cells × 59,537 genes. X : log1p(normalize_total(counts, target_sum = 10,000)), natural logarithm, float32 sparse matrix, as used in the analyses. layers["counts"] : integer UMI counts (int32 sparse matrix). obs :  Sample  (Reference = non-tumor, pancreas = PDAC),  group  (0 = Reference, 1 = pancreas),  celltype ,  donor ,  library ,  SourceFile ,  runs ,  n_runs_merged ,  total_counts ,  n_genes_by_counts . var : gene symbols. All genes are kept, because the normalization uses every gene. Cell type Non-tumor (HPAP) PDAC (GEO) Ductal cell 2,779 5,241 Endothelial cell 1,446 3,886 Stellate cell 1,231 2,510 Sources.  PDAC samples (38 samples contribute cells of these cell types) are from GEO series GSE154778, GSE205013, GSE212966, GSE214295 and GSE242230. Non-tumor samples are islet preparations of the Human Pancreas Analysis Program (HPAP) donors HPAP-077, HPAP-092, HPAP-099, HPAP-101 and HPAP-104; their count matrices were generated from the FASTQ files available through PANC-DB ( https://hpap.pmacs.upenn.edu ). Repeated sequencing runs of one HPAP donor library were summed by donor and cell barcode. Processing.  Samples were read and concatenated; cells with fewer than 600 detected genes, genes detected in fewer than three cells and cells outside the 2nd–98th percentile of detected genes were removed; expression was normalized to 10,000 counts per cell and log1p-transformed; samples were integrated with scVI; Leiden clusters (resolution 0.7) were annotated with decoupler and CellMarker marker sets, and cancer-labeled cells of non-tumor samples were reassigned after infercnvpy analysis. This file contains the three cell types analyzed; the integration embedding is not included. Important limitation.  Condition is completely confounded with data source and tissue preparation (all tumor samples from GEO, all non-tumor samples from HPAP islet preparations). The data are suitable for methodological comparisons, not for biological inference about tumor versus non-tumor expression. Verification.  Every row of  X  and  counts  is identical to the object used in the analyses, and DUET 1.0.0 run on the ductal cells reproduces the saved manuscript results (9,772 genes; maximum absolute difference in −log10 p 4.5 × 10⁻¹³). Software.  DUET 1.0.0:  https://github.com/Pahi95/duet ,  https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22801245 How to cite and acknowledge. Please cite this dataset, the DUET manuscript, the original GEO studies and the HPAP publications (Kaestner et al., Diabetes 2019; Shapira et al., Cell Metab 2022; Fasolino et al., Nat Metab 2022; Patil et al., Nat Metab 2023), and include the HPAP acknowledgement: "This study used data from the Human Pancreas Analysis Program (HPAP; RRID:SCR_016202; PMID: 31127054; PMID: 36206763). HPAP is part of the Human Islet Research Network (RRID:SCR_014393) consortium (UC4-DK112217, U01-DK123594, UC4-DK112232, and U01-DK123716)."
items.title: Pancreas single-cell RNA-seq analysis input for DUET: ductal, endothelial and stellate cells from PDAC (GEO) and non-tumor islet preparations (HPAP)

items.summary: World-action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot manipulation by jointly modeling future visual dynamics and robot actions. However, existing WAMs are trained predominantly on successful trajectories, making them prone to failure when real-world execution diverges from the learned dynamics. This issue is amplified in autoregressive WAMs, where execution errors become part of the causal history and continue to influence subsequent predictions. To this end, we introduce \method{}, a training-free framework that reformulates failure recovery as \emph{test-time scaling over causal histories}. This formulation decomposes recovery into three coupled decisions: \emph{when} to revise the causal history, \emph{where} to recover a reliable history prefix, and \emph{which} history configuration best supports subsequent execution. Specifically, \method{} realizes these decisions through three stages: 1) \textbf{Progress-Aware Recovery Trigger} detects persistent non-progress and triggers recovery only when the current execution state permits intervention; 2) \textbf{History-Prefix Recovery} identifies the unreliable history suffix, retrieves a historical anchor matching the current physical state, and reconstructs the causal KV state from the retained prefix while conditioning on the latest real observation; and 3) \textbf{Hypothesis Verification} compares the future continuations induced by complete-history, recovered-prefix, and full-reset hypotheses, and commits the best-supported hypothesis. Experiments in both simulated and real-world manipulation settings demonstrate consistent improvements in task success, while ablations confirm the contribution of each recovery stage.
items.title: Causal-History Test-Time Scaling for Failure Recovery in Autoregressive World-Action Models

items.summary: Reproducibility package supporting the numerical results, tables, and figures reported in “Attention Divergence Score: A Forensic Metric for Characterizing Model-State Tampering in Vision Transformers.” The release contains analysis code, protocol and provenance records, compact numerical result artifacts, selected per-image arrays, figure and table source data, and automated verification tools. It supports publication-result numerical and figure reproducibility; it does not include ImageNet image bytes, model checkpoint binaries, or large saved perturbation stores. Version 3.1.0 incorporates the final provenance synchronization, the recovered execution source required to fully specify the ROT180 structural-target analysis, and expanded direct verification of publication-reported results.
items.title: Attention Divergence Score: Reproducibility Package for Vision Transformer Model-State Tampering Experiments

items.summary: Derived tables and provenance registries supporting source-resolved mass absorption efficiency (MAE) estimates for wintertime brown carbon from residential solid-fuel combustion. Contents: (i) MAE estimates for 15 station pairs with block-bootstrap percentile intervals and trustworthiness grading; (ii) station metadata; (iii) per-dataset variable-group coverage tables; (iv) season-definition and denominator-threshold sensitivity tables; (v) AAE BC perturbation results; (vi) the denominator-rule audit log (per-station winter window hours, rule-excluded hours and retained hours); (vii) the 84-field variable dictionary of the harmonized master table v2; (viii) a per-dataset provenance registry (26 constituent datasets) recording authoritative archives, citations and access routes, together with a per-file DOI registry for the 64-station EBAS absorption compilation (2,913,812 hourly records, 2006-2025) and its audit trail; (ix) an integrity baseline of file checksums for independent verification. Primary hourly records are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original archives identified in the provenance registry. The harmonized master table itself is not included. Version v1.4.4 (2026-09-16) : adds the six-city Chinese pipeline results with verdict evidence, unified short-wave-benchmark spectral tables, per-scenario bootstrap coverage with the kappa=2 calibration, fair leave-one-station-out validation, the per-station analysis-object lock table, the Xi'an direct-perturbation identifiability domain, the China provenance registry, SFE station tables, and the corrected full-Mie conversion of the literature k range (proper small-particle form). The winter MAE table is superseded with single-version values. Version v1.4.5 (2026-09-17) : adds the consistent-source-dictionary leave-one-station validation with per-fold records, the two-batch independent coverage calibration with seed manifests, the Xi'an unified-baseline perturbation table, the seven-field per-station lock table v2, the recalculated literature coordinate table (proper small-particle form), and the forward-null probability accounting. The quantitative companion forcing table and figure are withdrawn pending deposition of the full radiative-chain inputs. Version v1.4.6 (2026-09-17) : adds the completed-source-dictionary validation (including Sh_Industry) with full per-fold predictions and coefficients, the timestamp-joined Xi'an clock perturbation with continuity assertion, the corrected coverage-scenario labelling, portable script entry points, and traceability notes for superseded analyses. Version v1.4.7 (2026-09-17) : adds the Beijing and Xi'an source-verification notes (instrument chains, inlet cuts, collection-efficiency treatment, receptor-model factor identification, sampling periods, verified against Xu et al. 2022 and Tian et al. 2021) and the verified China provenance registry. Version v1.4.8 (2026-09-17) : completes the six-city China provenance verification: Guanghan (Bao et al. 2023) and Lanzhou (Xu et al. 2016) verified against source publications, Harbin author-provided, Nanjing courtesy of co-authors, with the updated provenance registry and extended verification notes. Version v1.4.9 (2026-09-17) : adds the author-data correspondence section to the provenance registry and the extended verification notes covering all data contributors. Version v1.4.10 (2026-09-17) : final author-data correspondence with merged affiliations and the Yangtze River Delta data attribution in the provenance registry. Version v1.4.11 (2026-09-17) : corrects the Beijing factor chain to the HR-AMS (NR-PM1) analysis line, adds the field-level six-city verification status table, per-design validation denominators, the 452-hour clock-experiment baseline, and the reproducibility entry-point documentation with portable script examples.
items.title: Source-resolved brown carbon MAE estimates: derived tables, variable dictionary, and provenance registries

items.summary: Abstract This paper analyzes the computation of two-body energy transport and excitonic binding stability in a tight-binding framework on a honeycomb lattice from ab initio quantum Monte Carlo simulations. By tracking the evolution of single-particle and multi-particle states through a bipartite 18-site lattice grid, we evaluate the precise correlation functions and energy shifts relative to non-interacting thresholds across distinct spin-isospin channels. These discrete multi-body excitation dynamics are mapped and integrated directly into a unified Grand Unified Theory (GUT) Tone Theory model utilizing a flexible quantum lattice baseline. Through systematic auxiliary-field updates, we isolate the ground-state energies by cooling the grid down to absolute zero at the temporal midpoint of a cyclic timeline loop. The extracted negative energy shifts provide real-space structural verification of a deterministic, continuous attraction between unconfined particles, demonstrating how macroscopic thermodynamic decay profiles emerge from discrete whole-number steps within a conserved Hamiltonian framework. PACS Numbers: 71.35.-y, 02.70.Ss, 05.30.Fk, 11.15.Ha Keywords: TONE Framework, Quantum Monte Carlo, Honeycomb Lattice, Hubbard Model, Exciton Binding, Geometric Containment Copyright Notice: Copyright Pending © 2026 Anthony Santana. All Rights Reserved. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22803298
items.title: Tone Theory and Stability in Electron Excitation

items.summary: PIHR–RH XXXX reduced the remaining arithmetic obstruction in the Prime Integrator–Holonomy Recursion programme to a fixed-level funding problem formulated directly in critical-charge worldline coordinates. The central unresolved statement was the Critical-Charge Haar Funding theorem (CCHF), designed to combine transverse Prime-Spine funding, split–merge cancellation, proper-prime-power release control, and the coherent upper–upper sector before absolute values or quadratic symmetrization destroy the required directed information. The present continuation produces three further structural advances. First, the coarse upper–upper critical-charge transport admits an exact Hilbert-space contraction. If a prime adjunction   shifts a critical-charge partition by , then conditional averaging onto an arbitrary output partition contracts the normalized quadratic critical-charge energy by the factor 1/p.
items.title: Critical-Haar Overlap Contraction, Critical-Prefix Intertwining, and a Detailed Closure Blueprint for the Riemann Hypothesis (PIHR-RH-XXXXI)

items.summary: Peer sampling is a crucial primitive in distributed systems, used to manage overlays and disseminate information in large-scale scenarios such as permissionless blockchain systems. Its purpose is to maintain and regularly update a local and partial snapshot, or view, of the complete system's membership. These protocols are often targeted by malicious actors who aim to disrupt higher-level protocols. Typically, an adversary who controls a set of byzantine nodes attempts to manipulate how legitimate nodes perceive the presence of byzantine ones by increasing their representation in the view of honest nodes. While state-of-the-art byzantine-tolerant peer sampling protocols mitigate this bias, their effectiveness decreases significantly as the number of malicious nodes increases. This paper introduces AUPE, the first collaborative Byzantine-tolerant peer sampling protocol that leverages the presence of trusted nodes, such as Intel's SGX capable devices, to collaboratively track the spread of identifiers in the system and locally debias the representation of byzantine nodes. Simulations with 10,000 nodes demonstrate that AUPE outperforms state-of-the-art solutions, achieving nearperfect resilience even when faced with an adversary controlling 26% of the nodes. Overall, by including as few as 10% of trusted nodes, AUPE increases the tolerance of BRAHMS by up to 60% while limiting the impact of the adversary's attack, even when possessing up to 40% of the nodes.
items.title: AUPE: Collaborative byzantine fault-tolerant peer-sampling

items.summary: The Zodiac Z13 cipher, mailed 20 April 1970 beneath the words “My name is—,” contains thirteen positions but only eight ciphertext classes: one class occurs three times, three classes occur twice, and four occur once. Its brevity prevents a unique plaintext recovery without additional assumptions. This study therefore separates three questions that earlier work had blurred: what the raw repetition pattern forces, what a previously archived constraint branch forces, and what remains lexical completion. The exact ciphertext equalities are 1=12, 3=11, 5=7=9, and 8=13. Under the previously archived anchors NOT at positions 4–6 and MAN at positions 11–13, deterministic propagation yields: A?MNOTONO?MAN Only positions 2 and 10 remain free. The previously archived full trace AIMNOTONORMAN , corresponding to I and R at those positions, satisfies every required ciphertext equality under a deterministic homophonic-substitution model. It is therefore stronger than an unconstrained phrase fit, although those two letters are lexical completions rather than values uniquely forced by Z13. The paper additionally introduces an exact topology-preserving recurrence-geometry test. Across all 5,405,400 possible placements preserving Z13’s multiplicity structure of one triple, three pairs, and four singletons, only 19,656 satisfy the frozen conjunction observed in Z13: an arithmetic-progression triple, a doubleton span of at least 11 positions, mean repeated-class span of at least 7, and a common intersection among all repeated-class intervals. The exact frequency is therefore: 19,656 / 5,405,400 = 1/275 = 0.00363636 This result is explicitly treated as retrospective rather than as a preregistered discovery probability. The candidate also possesses unusually useful provenance. The exact trace AIMNOTONORMAN and segmentation AIM NOT O NORMAN were publicly archived on Zenodo on 2 November 2025 , more than two weeks before the author’s later Becker/Zodiac interpretive essays of 19–21 November 2025. This chronology excludes one specific post-hoc explanation—derivation of the cipher candidate from the later Becker interpretation—without establishing the candidate’s uniqueness or semantic intent. The study also reports the results of an explicit falsification campaign. Earlier claims that the Z340 corridor NANNANLA constituted a uniquely decoded Z13 closure signature are downgraded; the downstream NANNANLA → 71 → Z32 angle construction is withdrawn; and strong claims of universal fixed-alphabet continuity across Z408, Z13, Z340, and Z32 are narrowed. These retired branches are retained as adverse evidence rather than removed from the research history. The resulting claim is deliberately bounded: Z13 supports a reproducible structural candidate, AIMNOTONORMAN. It satisfies the cipher’s full repeated-symbol equality structure, arises from a documented pre-interpretation constraint branch, and is supported by non-generic recurrence geometry. It remains one independent external discriminator short of a definitive plaintext solution.
items.title: A Falsification-Driven Structural Reconstruction of the Zodiac Z13 Cipher
